headline: MassDOT approves $78.7 million contract for Mystic River walking and biking bridge
dek: The design-build award advances a planned car-free connection between Somerville’s Draw Seven Park and Everett’s Gateway Park trail network.
body: The Massachusetts Department of Transportation board approved a $78.7 million design-build contract Wednesday for a new pedestrian and bicycle bridge over the Mystic River, advancing a long-planned connection between Everett and Somerville.

The bridge will run between Draw Seven Park in Somerville and the Gateway Park trail and public boardwalk in Everett. MassDOT says the crossing is intended to close a gap in the area’s walking and biking network and give people a direct link to neighborhoods, businesses, transit and recreation on both sides of the river.

The project includes connections to existing shared-use paths, lighting, signs, landscaped approaches and riverfront improvements. Once construction is complete, the Department of Conservation and Recreation is expected to own and maintain the bridge, according to MassDOT.

The crossing is also designed to tie together the Northern Strand Trail, Mystic River Greenway, Malden River Greenway, Assembly Row and Everett’s Lower Broadway District. Streetsblog Massachusetts reported that the board voted unanimously on the contract, which covers both final design and construction.
author: NorthEast News Desk
